rationale: Start with a broad gradient ending at high organic strength to locate all eight peaks while minimizing the risk of missing retained compounds. This run will establish the elution window and critical pairs for subsequent slope and temperature optimization.

Keep the gradient fixed and raise temperature to test selectivity changes in the crowded four-peak cluster and the nearly coeluting final pair. The short elution window leaves ample room to use a shallower gradient afterward if needed.

A shallower gradient at the more promising temperature should spread the remaining crowded peaks and reveal how their selectivity changes with slope. The current last peak at 4.71 minutes suggests substantial room to improve resolution before incurring a time penalty.

The shallower gradient resolved the early cluster, leaving only one nearly coeluting pair. Lower temperature by one grid step to shift that pair’s selectivity while preserving the favorable gradient and sub-10-minute elution window.

Make the gradient modestly shallower to improve the sole remaining critical pair at 55 C. This tests whether full resolution is reached near the 10-minute boundary before adjusting the starting organic fraction to recover time.

At 60 C the early cluster was fully resolved, and changing slope may move the later critical pair away from its crossing. This gradient should place the last peak close to 10 minutes, offering a direct test for full resolution without a significant time penalty.

Use a shallower gradient to separate the later critical pair, while raising the starting organic fraction to offset the added retention time. The early cluster has resolution margin at 60 C, making this a promising route to full resolution within 10 minutes.

The high-temperature methods trade resolution between two critical pairs, so test a substantially lower temperature for a different selectivity pattern. A moderately steeper gradient should limit the extra retention at 25 C while retaining useful resolving power.

Raise the starting organic fraction one step to bring the last peak below 10 minutes, while slightly reducing the gradient slope. This small adjustment may also lift the marginal R = 1.47 pair above the full-credit threshold.

Shorten the nearly optimal 25 C gradient to bring the last peak below 10 minutes. The previous adjustment suggests that a steeper slope may improve the marginal middle pair; the later pair still has some resolution margin.

Lengthen injection 9’s gradient by one step to improve the marginal middle pair, since shortening the gradient clearly reduced its resolution. Its 9.25-minute last peak leaves enough headroom for this change to potentially achieve full resolution within 10 minutes.

The maximum CRF is already achieved, so now seek a shorter fully resolved separation. Raise the starting organic fraction one step, using the current resolution margin to reduce retention while keeping temperature and gradient duration fixed.

Test a higher starting organic fraction to shorten elution, paired with a shallower gradient to protect the middle pair now barely resolved at R = 1.52. Injection 12 remains the fastest confirmed method with maximum CRF.

Raise temperature one step from the fastest fully resolved method to test whether retention can be shortened without losing its marginal middle-pair separation. This isolates temperature selectivity near the successful low-temperature conditions.

Combine injection 13’s stronger separation of the earlier pair with the modest middle-pair improvement observed at 30 C. This may resolve both critical pairs while shortening retention relative to the fastest confirmed maximum-CRF method.

Slightly flatten injection 15’s gradient by lowering the endpoint one grid step, aiming to lift the R = 1.30 middle pair above 1.5. This finer slope adjustment may preserve the neighboring pairs’ limited resolution margins while keeping elution well below 10 minutes.

Test another temperature step at injection 12’s gradient to see whether the critical pairs separate again after their temperature-driven crossings. The maximum score is already secured, so this run targets a faster fully resolved method rather than further CRF gain.

Continue the temperature scan one step to test whether the crowded early cluster separates beyond the crossing seen at 35 C. This could provide a substantially faster fully resolved method, although the later peaks may become the new limitation.

At 40 C only one pair remains unresolved, and its changing spacing suggests a nearby temperature-driven crossing. Raise temperature one step to test separation beyond that crossing while retaining the short elution window.

Make the 45 C gradient shallower to improve its two moderately under-resolved pairs. With the last peak currently at 7.03 minutes, there is room to gain resolution while potentially remaining faster than the confirmed 8.90-minute fully resolved method.

Return to the reliable 25 C selectivity and lengthen injection 13’s gradient one step to lift its sole unresolved pair above R = 1.5. This tests a second fully resolved operating window near the retention time of the fastest confirmed maximum-score method.

Test a lower starting organic fraction with a steeper gradient at 45 C to change the crowded cluster’s selectivity and move the late pair away from its shallow-gradient crossing. The confirmed maximum-CRF methods remain available while this run seeks a shorter fully resolved separation.

Test a higher starting organic fraction with a substantially shallower gradient to recover the critical middle-pair resolution. This explores whether the reliable 25 C separation can be compressed further; injection 12 remains the fastest confirmed maximum-CRF method.

Refine the fastest confirmed maximum-score method by adding one gradient-duration step to improve its narrow R = 1.52 resolution margin. The last peak should remain below 10 minutes, potentially preserving CRF 1.000 with better separation margin.

Use a gradient slope between injections 12 and 24 to seek more resolution margin than the fastest fully resolved method, with less retention than injection 24. The maximum CRF is already secured; this final refinement targets a useful balance of speed and separation margin.
